verdict.summary: SOUND FOR THE DECLARED TRIAL SCOPE, WITH ONE REQUIRED TEST-EVIDENCE CORRECTION. No implementation defect was found in the asset algorithm or the Unix handle walk. The subject's own tests do not substantiate a number of rules the code implements and UNIT.md claims; those tests must be strengthened before they are cited as evidence for those rules.

requiredIssues.severity: required before these tests are cited as evidence
requiredIssues.title: Subject tests leave implemented and claimed normative rules unsubstantiated
requiredIssues.detail: Twelve non-equivalent mutants survive the subject suite: pin root/manifest path canonicality and scheme rule (M01, M02), assetManifestBytes minimum 1 (M03), sorted projection digest list (M05), lowercase-only digests (M06), 4096 code-point path bound (M07), over-reporting reader guard (M14), nonempty projection list (M18), schemaVersion const 1 (M19), completeness path admission (M21), compatibility over the whole list (M28), and O_CLOEXEC (P08), which UNIT.md states. UNIT.md's coverage sentence ('exact closed/lexical shape, schema compatibility, path/order/self-list rules') therefore overstates what the seven unit groups demonstrate. The lexical group asserts only is_err (non-vacuity comes from the open-list assertion), so a wrong refusal reason would not be detected.
requiredIssues.remedy: Add negative vectors that kill these mutants and assert the exact AssetError (the reviewer probe matrices in probe-src/ demonstrate one sufficient set), plus a descriptor-flag assertion for FD_CLOEXEC; or narrow the UNIT.md coverage statement. No implementation change is required.

pendingFinalIntegrationDuties.duty: Replace public FixturePin and verify_fixture_assets with the private compiled HostAssetPinV1 in reporting/assets.rs, including schemaVersion and the sole buildChannel, selected together with the real generated projection schema digest and actual offline bundle; development channel must be visible in version output; no caller path or pin may reach the rendering API.

Manifest parse profile: trial refuses above identity MAX_BYTES 4 MiB/32 containers while HostAssetPinV1 permits up to 9007199254740990 bytes. Final assembly must prove the actual manifest fits, or select a separately reviewed bounded private profile.

Implement the build/emission enumerator that completeness trusts: complete, no-symlink, target-semantics enumeration that also refuses non-regular entries (symlinks, FIFOs, sockets, devices) under assetRoot, since fixture_completeness only sees regular paths supplied to it; verify all bytes independently at build time.

Case-fold and Unicode-normalization aliasing on macOS targets (probe observed a case-insensitive filesystem): byte-unique manifest paths and byte-exact self-exclusion are insufficient for archive extraction onto such filesystems. Build/release assembly for macos-aarch64/macos-x86_64 rows must refuse paths that collide under case folding or normalization (among rows and against assetManifestPath) and check extracted trees. A case alias cannot bypass self-exclusion coverage (it would need a self-referential digest), but colliding rows would collapse at install. This is an owner input; no source amendment is made here.

Resource budgets: a member may declare up to 9007199254740990 bytes, all verified bytes are held in memory together, hashing is over the whole buffer after reading, and try_reserve does not prevent overcommit OOM termination on macOS/Linux. Establish actual bundle size, per-member and aggregate caps and host memory budgets; measured release hashing is ~400 MiB/s, debug ~33 MiB/s.

Projection binding: VerifiedBundle retains manifest digest/root/path but not the projection digest it was checked against (nor the pinned length). Product must make the projection a compile-time constant of the same owner or bind it into the verified type so a bundle cannot be reused for another projection.
If the renderer consumes a subset, introduce explicit checked selection; never ignore a missing selected asset.

D9 mapping only when an asset-consuming renderer is selected: DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED/delivery-required exit 4, RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT with retained RunId after commit, optional-surface failures leave the aggregate unchanged, no format downgrade.
Host implements the reporting-owned AssetSource using platform handles without a production reporting-to-platform edge; record the trial's dev-only edge under enforcement item 1.
Linux build and qualification of the adapter (not compiled for linux-gnu here); concurrent filesystem-race qualification beyond bounded probes.
Content-level offline behaviour (no network references inside asset bytes) belongs to built-browser offline/accessibility checks; the trial enforces the no-scheme rule on paths only.
Install-time provenance: include the report manifest and members in the TR-CORE signed inventory during release assembly (B14/B12); load-time pin remains additional.

advisories.detail: Returned File keeps O_NONBLOCK. Harmless for regular-file reads on macOS/Linux; consider clearing it with fcntl before returning or documenting it.

A device node at a leaf is opened (O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK) before fstat refuses it, so a driver open routine can run. This stays inside the trusted-install boundary (B10). Optional defence in depth: fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) pre-check, or O_PATH on Linux.

Error granularity is coarse (all lexical errors -> Shape; missing, extra and duplicate -> Unlisted). Adequate for the trial; final D9 detail mapping may want MANIFEST_SELF_LISTED/EXTRA_UNLISTED_FILE distinctions.

Evidence hygiene: the stated root test command does not run identity crate tests; cargo fmt result is not recorded in root-validation.json; cargo-clippy, clippy-driver, cargo-fmt and rustdoc are not tool-pinned (reviewer hashes recorded above).
Parent O_DIRECTORY, the parent fstat and subsequent-openat ENOTDIR overlap; M08's tail-length test is subsumed by canonical_path. These are not defects.
Build emission should write one canonical byte form (the parser admits whitespace and escapes, which the raw pin makes safe) to keep reproducible pins.

established: Untrusted manifest bytes cannot select paths or reach the parser unless the stored length and raw SHA-256 equal the pin; checked before parsing and before any member open.

Reads consume at most expected+1 bytes from growing or lying streams; allocation grows from actual data only; no partial bundle is returned; returned bytes are owned and unaffected by later source changes.
The handle walk from a retained root refuses symlinks at every segment, non-regular leaves and lexical traversal, does not block on FIFOs, and survives root and leaf substitution under the probes.
notEstablished: Who selected the root handle or whether the host binary is authentic (host TCB, B1/B10).
Protection against a hostile same-process AssetSource implementation; the trait is a trusted-host boundary, not a sandbox.
Hardlink refusal, mount-crossing policy, case/normalization aliasing policy, Linux behaviour, exhaustive race freedom, memory budgets, D9 integration, real bundle or release inventory.
